topic: Coca-Cola mailed millions of Americans a coupon for one free glass of Coke in the 1890s-1900s to build the habit nationwide
title: Coca-Cola Mailed Free Coke Coupons to Millions of Strangers
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script: This is a true business trick. Coca-Cola pulled it off over a century ago. They didn't aim for goodwill. They aimed for habit. In the 1890s and early 1900s, Coca-Cola mailed millions of Americans a simple coupon. This wasn't a small promotion. They flooded the nation. Each coupon offered one free glass of Coke. They sent these directly to total strangers, to homes across the country. The strategy was brilliant in its simplicity. Get people to try the product. Experience the unique taste. Form a new daily habit. This wasn't about a single free drink. It was about planting a seed. A seed for lifelong customer loyalty. This massive free giveaway built a national craving. It engineered a vast, dependable customer base. Coca-Cola didn't just sell a drink; they sold a habit. This is how you create an empire, one free coupon at a time. They taught America to love Coke. A truly sneaky deal that paid off for decades.
claims: Coca-Cola mailed millions of Americans a coupon for one free glass of Coke.
This occurred in the 1890s and early 1900s.
The coupons were sent to strangers.
The strategy aimed to build a habit.
The strategy aimed to create lifelong customers.
